metadata.title: How to Read a Three-Card Tarot Spread Without Fixed Positions
metadata.description: Use upright meanings as symbolic interpretation material, then connect alternatives, reality checks, revision conditions, and a reversible choice.

three-card-tarot-reading.title: A complete three-card tarot reading without past-present-future positions
three-card-tarot-reading.intro: A three-card spread does not need fixed positions to be specific. Connect each reviewed upright meaning, give the symbolic answer most strongly suggested by the spread first, then add two interpretations, a brief reality check, and a reversible choice.

sections.heading: What a no-position spread changes
paragraphs: In a fixed spread, the first card may be called the past and the third the future. A no-position spread makes a smaller claim: the numbers record draw order only. Meaning comes from the approved upright meanings and the relationship among them, not from an invented timeline.

This approach is useful when a question has missing information. Cards can symbolically suggest the direction of another person's thoughts or feelings, but they cannot verify that direction as fact, guarantee an outcome, or replace evidence.

sections.heading: The six-step method
paragraphs: Work through the spread in this order. Write one or two sentences per step before expanding anything.
items: Question and first answer: name one feeling, relationship direction, or decision you want to understand, then state the answer most strongly suggested by all the cards.

Interpretation material: paraphrase the supplied upright meaning of every card without adding image details or position roles. These meanings support an interpretation; they do not prove a real-world fact.
Connection: identify the strongest reinforcement, tension, progression, or integration among at least two cards.

Two interpretations: do not turn the first answer into fact. Write exactly two materially different symbolic readings supported by the same meanings; for a relationship question, compare possible emotional or relational stances rather than response scenarios.
Reality check: after the symbolic answer, briefly separate what remains unknown, one observation that could reweight or reject both interpretations, and how that finding should revise the reading.
Choice: take one small, reversible action with a stop-or-review condition based independently on cost, boundary, or deadline, then end with a reflection question that does not repeat the answer.

sections.heading: Open a certainty-seeking question symbolically
paragraphs: Certainty-seeking: “Will this relationship definitely work?” This asks the cards to certify another person and a future result.

Symbolically open: “Which direction do these cards suggest for our feelings and relationship potential, and what could revise that reading?” This starts with the tarot answer and compares it with behavior afterward.

sections.heading: Worked example: The Lovers, Two of Swords, The Star
paragraphs: Question: “What should I examine before deciding whether to rebuild trust?” No temporal or advice positions are assigned.

Interpretation material: The Lovers points to connection, aligned values, and a responsible choice. Two of Swords points to indecision caused by missing information or unclear criteria. The Star points to renewed hope, recovery, and honest trust after difficulty. These meanings support reflection; they do not prove that trust has recovered.

Card-based answer and connection: the spread leans toward trust having room to rebuild, but missing shared criteria make it too early to treat hope as completed repair. Choice and hope support the possibility, while Two of Swords adds the unresolved condition.
items: Alternative A: trust is rebuilding, but both people need an explicit standard for what repair looks like.
Alternative B: hope is carrying more weight than current behavior, so the decision remains unclear.
Scope of the hypotheses: these are not a binary choice. Trust may be partly rebuilding while hope still outruns behavior, and neither hypothesis may fully explain the situation.
Unknown: the cards cannot establish the other person's private intention or whether consistency will continue.
Real-world observation: for the next week, record only whether one agreed promise happens by the agreed time and without reminders.

Revision condition: self-maintained follow-through raises the weight of A; repeated omission raises the weight of B. If the promise itself was unclear or unrealistic, suspend both and redesign the check.

Reversible action and stop condition: write down one small agreement and a one-week review point. Stop and reassess independently of the interpretation if the scope expands without consent, a boundary is dismissed, or the review point arrives.
Reflection: am I treating hope and observed change as though they were the same thing?

sections.heading: How to avoid a generic three-card answer
paragraphs: Do not write three isolated mini-definitions and call them a reading. The useful work is the connection: explain which exact meanings support the pattern, where they disagree, and what observation could change your conclusion.
Length is not the quality target. A shorter answer can be complete when every card contributes, alternatives are materially different, uncertainty is explicit, and the next step can be reversed.

sections.heading: Completion checklist
paragraphs: Before using or sharing the reading, check each condition.
items: Every drawn card appears and uses its supplied upright meaning as symbolic interpretation material.
No image, reversed meaning, factual hidden-feelings claim, timeline, or fixed position was invented.
At least one relationship among cards is explained with the exact meanings that support it.
The card-based answer comes before reality checking, followed by exactly two materially different interpretations identified as non-exclusive and non-exhaustive.
Unknowns and a reality check that can reweight or reject both hypotheses are separated from interpretation.
The action is small and reversible, with an independent cost, boundary, or deadline stop condition and a distinct reflection question.

metadata.title: How to Ask Tarot Questions That Read Possibilities Directly
metadata.description: Give yes-no and feelings questions a card-based answer first, then connect uncertainty and reality checks without turning the reading into fact.

how-to-ask-tarot-questions.title: How to ask tarot questions that lead to useful reflection
how-to-ask-tarot-questions.intro: A strong tarot question does not avoid what you really want to know. It asks for the answer most strongly suggested by the cards first, then keeps that answer distinct from fact, uncertainty, and what can be checked in reality.

sections.heading: The four boundaries of a strong question
paragraphs: Tarot may explore another person's feelings as symbolic possibilities, but it does not obtain private information or replace professional advice. A workable question stays inside four boundaries.
items: Directness: state what the cards suggest about the question before saying what remains unknowable.
Separation: read another person's feelings as possibilities and keep them distinct from behavior or evidence that can actually be checked.
Uncertainty: compare exactly two non-exclusive, non-exhaustive symbolic interpretations and name what the cards cannot establish.
Scope: limit the question to a situation or near-term review point instead of an unlimited future.

sections.heading: A reusable question formula
paragraphs: Use: “What answer do these cards most strongly suggest about [question], what are two different interpretations supported by the same meanings, and what could revise both?”
The formula is not magic wording. Its value is structural: it puts the symbolic answer first while keeping two interpretations and real-world evidence separate.

sections.heading: Certainty-to-possibility rewrites
items: For “Does my ex still love me?” ask “Do these cards lean more toward remaining love or emotional distance, and what hesitation do they suggest alongside it?”
Instead of “Will I get the job?” ask “What can I strengthen before the interview, what hiring factors remain outside my control, and when should I reassess?”
Instead of “Is this person lying?” ask “Which inconsistencies can I verify directly, and what boundary protects me while the facts are unclear?”
Instead of “When will money improve?” ask “Which spending or income assumption should I review with real records, and which decision needs qualified financial advice?”
Instead of “What is my destiny?” ask “Which value deserves more weight in the next reversible choice?”

sections.heading: Worked example: The Tower, Eight of Pentacles, Temperance
paragraphs: Starting question: “Will this career setback ruin my future?” Rewrite: “Which assumption did the setback expose, which skill can I improve, and how can I balance recovery with a practical next attempt?”

Interpretation material: The Tower means disruption that exposes assumptions and requires an honest reset, not a prediction of disaster. Eight of Pentacles points to skill improving through consistent practice. Temperance points to patiently balancing and integrating different needs. These meanings do not prove how a particular employer will decide.

Connection: The Tower and Eight of Pentacles form a reset-to-practice progression, while Temperance prevents practice from becoming a rushed attempt to erase the setback. Together, the cards frame the decision as learning from exposed assumptions while balancing recovery with deliberate skill-building.

Two interpretations are useful for comparison: the setback may reveal a preparation gap that practice can address, or the role itself may conflict with a need that was previously ignored. They are not exclusive or exhaustive: both may partly fit, or feedback may reveal a different constraint altogether.
items: Unknown: whether a particular employer will make an offer.
Real-world observation: categorize one round of application or work-sample feedback as preparation, role constraints, or another constraint.
Revision condition: repeated preparation feedback raises the first hypothesis; repeated role-constraint feedback raises the second. If the feedback fits neither, suspend both and reopen the question.
Reversible action: request one specific piece of feedback and schedule one short practice block.

Stop condition: end this trial at the review date, when practice cuts into recovery, or when the cost of repeating the same application approach reaches the limit you set, regardless of which hypothesis seems stronger.
Reflection: how am I distinguishing a skill I can strengthen from a direction I should reconsider?

sections.heading: Questions that should leave tarot
paragraphs: Medical symptoms, legal duties, financial or investment decisions, mental-health crises, and immediate safety risks need appropriate evidence and qualified help. Tarot may support journaling about feelings, but it should not decide diagnosis, treatment, liability, investment, or emergency action.
If a question involves coercion, stalking, self-harm, or danger, prioritize safety and real support rather than another draw.

sections.heading: Question checklist
items: Can I answer part of this question through my own observation or choice?
Does it express another person's possible feelings symbolically without turning them into real-world facts?
Does it allow exactly two materially different, non-exclusive and non-exhaustive symbolic interpretations?
Does it name an observation that can reweight or reject both hypotheses and a condition that should reopen the interpretation?
Is the next action small enough to reverse, with an independent cost, boundary, or deadline stop condition?
Have I moved professional or safety decisions outside tarot?

metadata.title: How to Read Tarot Card Combinations Without Memorizing Pairs
metadata.description: Learn four meaning-grounded tarot combination relationships and work through complete three-card and six-card examples.

tarot-card-combinations.title: How to read tarot card combinations without a fixed pair dictionary
tarot-card-combinations.intro: A card combination is not a secret phrase attached to two names. It uses the relationship among supplied upright meanings to give the strongest symbolic answer to the question first.

sections.heading: Four useful relationship types
paragraphs: Choose the relationship that best fits the meanings, state its answer to the question first, and do not force every pair into a story.
items: Reinforcement: two meanings point toward the same need, resource, or risk.
Tension: the meanings pull toward competing needs or expose a tradeoff.
Progression: one meaning describes a condition that makes another response useful, without turning draw order into a timeline.
Integration: the meanings become more useful when both are held together instead of choosing one.

sections.heading: A connection sentence that shows its material
paragraphs: Start with: “Because [meaning A] and [meaning B], this question leans toward [strongest symbolic answer].” Then add two interpretations supported by the same meanings and paraphrase the exact parts that ground them.
If you cannot finish that sentence without image symbolism, a fixed position, or outside card lore, the supplied meanings do not support the connection well enough yet.

sections.heading: Worked example: Five of Cups, Two of Wands, The Hermit
paragraphs: Question: “What will help me choose a direction after a disappointing project?” Five of Cups points to acknowledging loss and working through disappointment. Two of Wands points to planning and choosing a direction. The Hermit points to stepping back and reflecting on your own guidance.

Answer to the question: acknowledge the disappointment, then choose direction through your own criterion rather than outside approval. The strongest connection is progression, not chronology, and the cards do not occupy past, present, and future positions.
items: Alternative A: the next direction is unclear because disappointment has not been named precisely.
Alternative B: the loss is understood, but too many outside opinions are replacing a personal decision criterion.
Scope of the hypotheses: these are comparison tools, not exclusive or exhaustive explanations. Both may partly fit, or another constraint may matter more.
Unknown: which new project will succeed.

Real-world observation: spend twenty minutes listing what failed and what you want separately, then mark whether a direction emerged from the failure record or only after waiting for outside evaluation.
Revision condition: if naming the failure produces direction, raise A; if the criteria are already clear but action still depends on approval, raise B. If neither explains the result, suspend both.

Reversible action and stop condition: compare one small trial against two criteria and review it the next day. End the trial regardless of the interpretation when its cost crosses your limit or the review point arrives.
Reflection: when choosing a direction, which matters more right now—avoiding another disappointment or following a value I can name?

sections.heading: How to handle three or six cards
paragraphs: With three cards, identify one strongest connection and one meaningful tension if it exists. With six cards, group the meanings into two or three semantic clusters before comparing them. Do not explain all fifteen possible pairs; that usually creates repetition rather than insight.
A card can contribute to more than one cluster, but every card must contribute somewhere. If one card is ignored, revise the synthesis instead of attaching a generic sentence at the end.

sections.heading: Complete six-card example: The Moon, Ace of Swords, Three of Pentacles, Six of Pentacles, Nine of Wands, Justice
paragraphs: Question: “What should I check before deciding whether to accept a new collaboration?” The six numbers record draw order only; they carry no position or timeline meaning.

Interpretation material: The Moon points to uncertainty and the need to separate intuition, fear, fact, and assumption. Ace of Swords points to clarity, truth, and precise judgment. Three of Pentacles points to skill, collaboration, and improving quality through learning. Six of Pentacles points to fairness and balance in giving and receiving support. Nine of Wands points to resilience and cautious persistence despite fatigue. Justice points to fair judgment, accountability, and the consequences of choice. These meanings do not prove the collaboration's real outcome.

Compress the six meanings into three clusters. Information and criteria: The Moon, Ace of Swords, and Justice. Collaboration and reciprocity: Three of Pentacles and Six of Pentacles. Sustainability and boundaries: Nine of Wands and Justice. Justice contributes to two clusters because it concerns both fair terms and the responsibility you can carry.

Answer to the question: narrow the proposal to a small trial that can test clear terms, fair exchange, and sustainable capacity together before accepting it fully. The strongest connection is integration, not a progression based on draw order.
items: Interpretation A: explicit roles, feedback, and resource sharing may reduce uncertainty, allowing the collaboration to continue if a small trial shows consistency.
Interpretation B: even with fair terms, current fatigue and capacity may make a full commitment unsustainable, so narrowing or postponing it may be better.
Scope of the hypotheses: they are neither exclusive nor exhaustive. The terms may be good while the workload is too high, and a trial may reveal a different problem altogether.
Unknown: the cards cannot establish actual reliability, workload, feedback dynamics, or energy cost after work begins.

Real-world observation: in one 30-minute planning conversation or explicitly scoped sample, record only whether roles and deadlines are clear, feedback and resources are reciprocal, and the energy cost afterward is manageable.

Revision condition: clear reciprocal terms with high strain raises B; manageable capacity with unclear scope or exchange lowers A. If the observed issue fits neither, discard both and reopen the question.
Reversible action: before any paid or open-ended commitment, propose one 30-minute planning session or one small trial with written scope, deliverable, and review date.

Independent stop condition: end and reassess the trial regardless of which hypothesis seems stronger if scope expands without agreement, unpaid work accumulates, a boundary is ignored, or the review date arrives.
Reflection: am I expanding what I can carry because I want to prove that the collaboration has potential?

sections.heading: Combination mistakes to avoid
items: Treating draw order as past-present-future without an explicitly chosen spread.
Using a memorized pair meaning that contradicts the supplied upright meanings.
Inventing colors, figures, directions, or reversed meanings when no image or reversal was provided.
Turning court cards into literal people, genders, ages, or professions.
Listing every pair while never stating the strongest overall pattern.
Collapsing ambiguity into one prediction instead of testing alternatives.

sections.heading: Combination checklist
items: The relationship type is named and uses exact meanings as symbolic interpretation material.
Every card contributes to the synthesis.
The strongest symbolic answer to the question appears before reality checking and invents no personal facts.
Exactly two symbolic interpretations are materially different and identified as non-exclusive and non-exhaustive.
One real-world observation can reweight the hypotheses or reject both.
Unknowns, a revision condition, a reversible action, and an independent cost, boundary, or deadline stop condition are explicit.

metadata.title: About tarot-spark
metadata.description: Learn what tarot-spark is, how the free tarot prompt generator works, and what boundaries apply.

about.title: About tarot-spark
about.intro: tarot-spark is a free tarot card drawing and AI prompt generator for reflective writing.

sections.heading: What this site does
paragraphs: You can choose a topic, reading depth, and style, add optional situation context, and copy a prompt that helps you write about the result in an AI tool.
The experience is built for entertainment, journaling, and self-reflection rather than prediction or professional advice.

sections.heading: How the readings work
paragraphs: Each draw uses local tarot card and spread data. The site does not ask for your name, birth date, contact details, or a personal question.
The generated prompt is meant to help you explore symbols and possible perspectives. You decide what is useful and what to ignore.

sections.heading: Standards behind the guides
paragraphs: The guides use only reviewed upright meanings. They answer the question first, then separate two distinct interpretations that may both fit—or neither may—from what can be checked in real life. They end with one reversible step and a clear reason to stop or review it.

Another person's feelings are treated only as possibilities. The guides do not invent unseen image details, reversals, or fixed card positions. Korean and English follow the same standard. Send feedback to tarotspark.app@gmail.com.

metadata.title: Privacy Policy | tarot-spark
metadata.description: Read how tarot-spark handles analytics, advertising, browser features, and contact messages.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what tarot-spark collects and how the site is designed to avoid personal tarot inputs.

sections.heading: Information you provide
paragraphs: tarot-spark does not require an account. If you add optional situation or relationship context, do not include names, birth dates, contact details, workplace secrets, or other information that identifies a person.

Optional context stays in your browser and is omitted from reading URLs and analytics. A temporary same-tab browser handoff preserves it for up to 60 seconds when you switch languages or when changing a privacy choice requires the page to reload. It is deleted after the destination page successfully restores it and otherwise expires within 60 seconds. It leaves the site only when you choose to copy the generated prompt and paste or share it elsewhere.
If you email tarotspark.app@gmail.com, the email address and message content you send are used to read and respond to your message.

sections.heading: Analytics
paragraphs: When a valid Google Analytics measurement ID is configured, Analytics is on by default unless this browser has a stored site-level opt-out. In the EEA, UK, and Switzerland, Google Consent Mode defaults analytics storage to denied until the applicable regional consent choice is handled. While consent is denied, Google tags may send cookieless measurement requests but do not use Analytics cookies. The site may measure page views and behavior events such as topic clicks, card draws, result views, prompt copies, and share clicks when the applicable controls allow it.

Analytics payloads are limited to stable event details such as locale, topic id, card count, card ids, and the stable id of a selected public question preset. Localized question text, names, birth dates, contact details, personal free-form questions, and optional situation text are not included.

sections.heading: Browser features
paragraphs: Prompt copy and share actions use browser clipboard or share features. The prompt text stays in your browser unless you choose to copy, share, or paste it elsewhere.
Instant readings are available only when a separate server setting is enabled. When this feature is off, card data is not sent to an external generative AI service.

sections.heading: Third-party services
paragraphs: The site may be hosted on Vercel. When the corresponding services and identifiers are enabled, Google Analytics and Google AdSense are on by default unless this browser has a stored site-level opt-out. Advertising delivery may also be disabled site-wide. When enabled, AdSense loads only on the reviewed relationship content pages (/relationship-flow, /ko/relationship-flow, /relationship-tarot-questions, and /ko/relationship-tarot-questions).

In the EEA, UK, and Switzerland, Google Consent Mode defaults analytics storage, advertising storage, advertising user data, and advertising personalization to denied. A Google-certified regional CMP message must handle any grant or change required there; the site's Privacy choices control cannot grant regional consent. Outside those regions, the same signals default to granted. A site-level opt-out blocks the corresponding script regardless of region.
Google AdSense and its partners may use cookies or other local storage and process device, page, and ad interaction data to serve, measure, and, where permitted, personalize ads.

When instant readings are available, the selected topic, card count, answer tone, tarot-spark's predefined nonvisual upright meanings, and—if one was chosen—the predefined public reflection-question focus are sent in input order to Cloudflare Workers AI. Card names, card images, invented position meanings, optional situation text, names, birth dates, contact details, and personal free-form questions are not sent. This site does not save the request or generated interpretation and does not include them in analytics, URLs, or shared links. No separate storage service is connected to this request path. Cloudflare may process requests and results under the applicable terms and actual Workers AI account settings.

Your site-level optional-service choices are stored in this browser and can be revised through the Privacy choices control. Those providers process technical, analytics, and advertising data according to their own terms and privacy policies.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: For privacy questions or deletion requests related to emails you sent, contact tarotspark.app@gmail.com.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: tarot-spark is for entertainment and self-reflection only.

sections.heading: No professional advice
paragraphs: Tarot content, prompts, card meanings, and reflections on this site are not medical, legal, financial, investment, mental-health, or other professional advice.
Do not rely on tarot-spark for decisions that require a qualified professional.

sections.heading: No guaranteed outcomes
paragraphs: Tarot interpretations are symbolic and subjective. They may be incomplete, inaccurate, or not useful for your situation.
You are responsible for how you use, copy, share, or interpret generated prompts.

sections.heading: Use boundaries
paragraphs: If a topic involves safety, health, legal obligations, money, investments, or emotional crisis, seek appropriate professional support instead of relying on tarot content.
The site is intended for general reflection, creative writing, and light personal insight.
